I've been working this land for 30 years. I know this soil. I know what it needs and what it doesn't. My plot is small — 1.1 mu — so I can manage it mostly by myself, especially since my son and daughter-in-law are working in the city. They send money back, which helps, so I don't need to squeeze every jin out of this land. But I'm not going to neglect it either. This is wheat-maize country. That's what I plant. That's what my parents planted.

**Wheat (winter):** I'll plant the whole 1.1 mu in wheat come October. I always use an improved variety — I switched from saving my own seed years ago when I saw how much better the yields were with Jimai varieties. Basal fertilizer goes in before sowing, then I'll top-dress nitrogen at jointing. Three irrigations: 冬灌 before the ground freezes, then at jointing, then at grain filling. I'll spray herbicide in early spring when the weeds come up, and one round of fungicide when I see the weather getting humid — powdery mildew and rust can take a lot if you ignore them.

**Maize (summer):** Soon as the wheat comes off in June, I'll go straight to planting maize. No need to deep plow — I'll do rotary tillage to break up the stubble. I use hybrid seed, same brand I've trusted for the past several years. Summer gets rain here so I won't need to pump as much, maybe twice — once at germination if it's dry, once at silking. I top-dress nitrogen heavily when the plants are knee-high. I spray herbicide right after planting and maybe one more time for corn borers if I see them.
